execution_form.steps_4_5_6_8: the file is ONE transaction: begin; set local lock_timeout (2s; 1s for step 8, the hot gallery table); set local statement_timeout = '60s'; set local search_path = public, pg_catalog; lock table <the tables the step changes> in share update exclusive mode; THEN the catalogue fingerprint guard (so a policy change by another session is either finished and seen, or the lock wait fails and nothing changes); the changes; a postcondition on the exact fingerprint; commit. The guard accepts only the live state read on 14.11.2026 (or, idempotently, the file's own result) and refuses before any change otherwise; the rollback accepts only the state its apply produced and its postcondition requires the exact state before the apply (so a rollback that is not exact fails instead of passing). On a lock timeout nothing has changed: STOP and inspect (pg_locks, pg_stat_activity) and do not resend automatically (ZURIEL's adopted rule, 14.11.2026). Lock facts measured on PostgreSQL 16 and 17: CREATE/ALTER/DROP POLICY take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on the table (running readers delay them, new readers queue behind them, for at most the lock timeout); GRANT/REVOKE take no table lock, so a grant made by another session between the guard and the commit is not excluded by the lock (the postcondition sees a grant committed before it)
execution_form.steps_2_7_10: each change is one statement (a DO block, or one md5-guarded patch call): atomic by construction; the files are unchanged since the reviews (CR-X1 for step 2)
execution_form.send_as: one complete call per file, without edits
execution_form.before_each_step: read the fingerprints/preconditions of that step again (this file, fields live_precondition and guard) - the files also check them themselves
